newsitem.title: UK: FTSE 100 up to day's best on buoyant drugs, oils.
newsitem.headline: FTSE 100 up to day's best on buoyant drugs, oils.

text.p: UK's FTSE 100 share index jumped by more than one percent on Tuesday, lifted by buoyant pharmaceutical and oil stocks, dealers said.
By 1041 GMT, the leading blue chip index climbed 53.0 points to 4,948.7, the day's best level.
The push to the day's peak came after British Petroleum Co Plc posted better-than-expected second quarter results and announced an unexpected share buyback.

Leading gains in the oil sector, the BP stock added 21-1/2p to 843-1/2, having hit a record at 847p, after the group second quarter replacement cost net profits of 740 million stg, excluding exceptionals.
Higher crude oil prices and a good performance in the sector's ADRs overnight had underpinned gains in the group before BP published its results.
Elsewhere, pharmaceutical shares surged after their ADRs rallied overnight.
The two sectors accounted for more than half of the FTSE 100 point gain. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 5106
